headerBody: Argentina: Tourist Scams maps the exact plays that work the Calle Florida sidewalk, the Retiro and San Telmo taxi ranks, the Cerro Campanario lookouts above Bariloche, and the El Calafate glacier-tour windows. Every entry is documented against Argentine police reporting — Policía Federal (911) and the Comisaría Turística tourist police — plus Defensa del Consumidor rules, r/Argentina and r/solotravel reports, and verified Argentine news, then drawn in a warm Quino-style cartoon so you recognize the setup before it reaches the pitch.
quadHead: Four ways Argentina catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Plaza de Mayo Bird-Poop Distraction
quad.tl: Walking near Plaza de Mayo or the Caminito strip in La Boca, something wet hits your shoulder — mustard, ketchup, a chocolate-syrup “bird dropping” — and a kindly stranger materializes with napkins to help you clean it; while their hands are on you, a teammate lifts your wallet, phone, or passport.

quad.title: The Cerro Campanario Smash-and-Grab
quad.tl: A two-person team on a motorcycle waits at the Cerro Campanario lower parking lot; the moment a rental car parks and the driver walks toward the chairlift, the passenger window is gone in fifteen seconds — and the camera bag, laptop, and backpack go with it before you reach the lift.

quad.title: The Perito Moreno VIP Bait-and-Switch
quad.tl: An Av. del Libertador agency sells a “Big Ice Glacier Day with VIP Helicopter” at USD 700 per person; the actual operator is Hielo y Aventura, the direct rate is USD 380 for Big Ice plus USD 32 park entrance plus USD 25 transfer (USD 437 total), and the “VIP” tier you paid for is the same shared bus everyone else is on.

quad.title: The Tachero Cloned-Meter Loop
quad.tl: A street taxi flagged at random in Retiro or San Telmo runs a meter cloned to 2–3× the legal tariff, takes the long way through the autopista, then swaps your clean 10,000-peso note for a counterfeit and demands a “real” replacement — turning a legitimate ARS3,500 ride into ARS10,000+.

body: Argentina: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Argentine police reporting — Policía Federal (911) and the Comisaría Turística tourist police — Defensa del Consumidor rules, r/Argentina and r/solotravel reports, and verified Argentine news. Sourced and re-reported, not recycled from blog lists.

66 specific scams across Buenos Aires, Mendoza, Bariloche, El Calafate, Ushuaia and 7 more cities — the Calle Florida “¡cambio!” arbolito, the counterfeit-peso switchback, the bird-poop distraction, the tachero cloned meter, the glacier-tour “VIP” bait-and-switch. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Spanish phrases that shut them down, written phonetically so you can show them on your phone.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched every year, and the current edition sits in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Argentina relaxed, not braced.
